PAC: Political Action Committee. A 527 organization that pools campaign contributions from members and donates those funds to campaigns for or against candidates, ballot initiatives, or legislation.
Super PAC: Independent Expenditure-Only Committee. These committees may receive unlimited contributions from individuals, corporations, labor unions and other PACs for the purpose of financing independent expenditures and other independent political activity.
Cash on Hand: The total amount of money a campaign or committee has in the bank at the end of a reporting period.
Schedule A: Itemized receipts. This includes contributions from individuals, PACs, and party committees.
Schedule B: Itemized disbursements. This covers the expenditures made by the committee, including operating expenses, transfers, and contributions to other committees.
Schedule E: Independent Expenditures. Money spent by Super PACs or other organizations to support or oppose a candidate, without coordinating with the candidate's campaign.
Form 3X (F3X): The Report of Receipts and Disbursements for a Political Committee other than an Authorized Committee. Used by PACs and party committees.
Form 3 (F3): The Report of Receipts and Disbursements for an Authorized Committee. Used by House and Senate campaigns.
Form 3P (F3P): The Report of Receipts and Disbursements for an Authorized Committee. Used by Presidential campaigns.
Dark Money: Political spending by nonprofit organizations (e.g., 501(c)(4) groups) that are not required to disclose their donors. While the FEC tracks their expenditures, the source of their funding remains hidden.
